text:
Ivy (net-arch): quick sync after the v2 controlplane RFC. we need a safe migration path for private endpoints that avoids traffic doubling and preserves source-IP for NAT customers.
Marc (infra): 👍 ops constraint: some customers enforce src-ip ACLs. what’s the minimal continuity window we can offer?
Ivy (net-arch): propose short dual-advertise + session affinity tokens. default affinity_ttl=120s; configurable per-tenant. expose migration_mode=canary|force|hold.
Lea (onboarding): onboarding asks for an opt-out flow and a CLI helper. `rctl tenant migrate --id TID --mode canary --dry-run`?
Ivy (net-arch): exactly. server fallback: if v2 handshake fails 3 times, pin tenant to v1 for 10m and emit cp_v2_fallback metric.
Hector (eng-sre): add metrics: cp_v2_attempts_total, cp_v2_fallbacks_total, cp_v2_handshake_ms hist. alert if >0.5% tenants fallback for 10m. also probe token refresh latency.
Gus (product): docs one-liner: "No planned downtime; persistent connections may see brief IP continuity changes. contact SE for strict ACLs." include migration FAQ.
Marc (infra): technical: v2 uses signed route tokens (5-6m TTL). need a tiny token-renewer for on-prem/air-gapped installs or require relay-agent. renewer should expose /health and write tokens to a local socket.
Lea (onboarding): we'll package a small static binary and provide install instructions. CLI will support opt-out and dry-run.
Ivy (net-arch): migration steps (summary): 1) set migration_mode=canary 2) deploy token-renewer or enable relay-agent 3) dual-push DNS (apex TTL=45s) for ~8m 4) monitor metrics and promote to force if clean.
deploy-bot: token-renewer v0.1 -> staging (sha: c0ffee)
